tagline: Up the slow bayou from Morgan City to Arnaudville.
intro: From Morgan City the byway hugs Bayou Teche through St. Mary, Iberia and St. Martin parishes as far as Arnaudville. The bayou is 125 miles long and was once the main course of the Mississippi. Its name may come from a Chitimacha word for snake, for the way it twists and turns.

After the Louisiana Purchase sugar planters lined it with big houses, and loggers took cypress out of the Atchafalaya Basin beyond. In the Civil War Union gunboats came up it twice after the J. A. Cotton, a Confederate gunboat armored in part with railroad iron.

moments.title: Charenton
moments.text: In 1915 Sarah Avery McIlhenney bought the remaining Chitimacha land at a sheriff's sale and handed it over in trust for the tribe, whose women weave double-walled baskets of river cane.

moments.title: Shadows-on-the-Teche
moments.text: Built in 1834 for the sugar planter David Weeks, the red brick house in New Iberia stands 20 feet above the bayou behind eight white Tuscan columns.

moments.title: Breaux Bridge
moments.text: In 1799 Firmin Breaux hung a footbridge of rope and planks across the Teche between two live oaks, and people giving directions said go to Breaux's bridge until the town took the name.
